translations.text: Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, to go before these solemnities with a service the readier as you show the beginning of our redemption to stand in them. Through Christ our Lord.
Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, to be quickened by the birth of your Only-Begotten Son recounted anew, by whose heavenly mystery we are fed and given drink. Who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

May the offering of this day's feast be pleasing to you, O Lord, we beseech you, that through these most holy exchanges we may be found in the likeness of him in whom our nature is with you. Who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

propers.incipit: Da nobis, quaesumus, Domine Deus noster
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

translations.text: Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord our God, that we who rejoice to keep the birth of our Redeemer may by a worthy manner of life deserve to come to fellowship with him. Who lives and reigns for ever and ever.
Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that while we are bathed in the new light of your incarnate Word, that which shines by faith in our minds may blaze out in what we do. Through our Lord.

May our gifts, we beseech you, O Lord, come forth fitted to the mysteries of this day's birth, that as he who was born man shone out as God also, so this earthly substance may confer on us what is divine. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.incipit: Da nobis, Domine, Filii tui nativitatem
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

translations.text: O God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human nature and still more wonderfully restored it, grant us, we beseech you, to be sharers in the godhead of him who deigned to become a partaker of our humanity. Who lives and reigns with you.

May the offering of this day's solemnity be acceptable to you, O Lord, by which both the perfect atonement of our reconciliation went forth and the fullness of divine worship was bestowed on us. Through Christ our Lord.
Grant, merciful God, that as the Saviour of the world, born this day, is for us the author of the divine birth, so he may himself be the giver of immortality. Who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

translations.text:
Forth to the paschal Victim, Christians, bring
Your sacrifice of praise:

The Lamb redeems the sheep;
And Christ, the Sinless One,
Hath to the Father sinners reconcil’d.

Together, Death and Life
In a strange conflict strove;
The Prince of Life, who died,
Now lives and reigns.

What thou sawest, Mary, say,
As thou wentest on the way.

I saw the tomb wherein the Living One had lain;
I saw his glory as He rose again;
Napkin and linen clothes, and Angels twain:
Yea, Christ is risen, my hope, and He
Will go before you into Galilee.

We know that Christ indeed has risen from the grave:
Hail, thou King of Victory!
Have mercy, Lord, and save.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts, and guidance/propers-for-agents.md
reserves the choice among them to the maintainer. This row records that the
maintainer named Caswall; it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts, and guidance/propers-for-agents.md
reserves the choice among them to the maintainer. This row records that the
maintainer named Caswall; it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

translations.text: Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, that the course of the world may be directed for us in peace by your ordering, and that your Church may rejoice in tranquil devotion. Through our Lord.

propers.incipit: Deus, qui offerenda tuo nomini tribuis
propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

translations.text: O God, who grant us what we are to offer to your name, and reckon what is offered to the devotion of our service, we beg your mercy, that what you supply as the ground of merit you may bountifully grant to profit us unto our reward. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.incipit: Cantabo Domino, qui bona tribuit mihi

propers.name: Entrance Antiphon

translations.text: O God, whose providence does not fail in what it appoints, we humbly entreat you to put away from us all that is harmful and to grant us all that will profit us. Through our Lord.

masses.name: Tenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.incipit: Deus, a quo bona cuncta procedunt
propers.name: Collect

translations.text: O God, from whom all good things proceed, grant to your suppliants that by your inspiration we may think what is right and by your governance may do it. Through our Lord.
May your healing work, O Lord, in mercy set us free from our own crookedness and lead us on to what is right. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Eleventh Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.incipit: Deus, qui humani generis utramque substantiam
propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

translations.text: O God, who quicken both substances of the human race by the nourishment of these present gifts and renew them by their sacrament, grant, we beseech you, that their help may be wanting neither to our bodies nor to our minds. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.name: Communion Antiphon

propers.name: Prayer after Communion

masses.name: Twelfth Sunday in Ordinary Time

translations.text: Make us, O Lord, hold always both the fear and the love of your holy name, for you never withdraw your governance from those whom you establish in the firmness of your love. Through our Lord.

propers.incipit: Suscipe, Domine, sacrificium placationis et laudis
propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

propers.incipit: Sacri Corporis et Sanguinis pretiosi alimonia
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

masses.name: Thirteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

translations.text: O God, who graciously bring about the effect of your mysteries, grant, we beseech you, that our service may be made fit for these sacred gifts. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Fourteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

translations.text: May this offering, O Lord, consecrated to your name, cleanse us, and carry us over, day by day, into the manner of life of heaven. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.name: Communion Antiphon

propers.incipit: Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis
propers.name: Communion Antiphon

translations.text: Filled with gifts so great, O Lord, grant, we beseech you, that we may lay hold of what brings salvation and never cease from your praise. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Fifteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.incipit: Ego autem cum iustitia apparebo in conspectu tuo
propers.name: Entrance Antiphon

propers.incipit: Deus, qui errantibus, ut in viam possint redire
propers.name: Collect

propers.incipit: Qui manducat meam carnem et bibit meum sanguinem
propers.name: Communion Antiphon

translations.text: Now that we have received your gifts, we beseech you, O Lord, that with each celebration of the mystery the effect of our salvation may increase. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Sixteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

translations.text: O God, who ratified the diversity of the sacrifices of the Law in the perfection of one sacrifice, receive this sacrifice from your devoted servants, and hallow it with the same blessing as the gifts of Abel, that what each has offered to the honour of your majesty may profit all unto salvation. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.incipit: Ecce sto ad ostium et pulso
propers.name: Communion Antiphon

propers.incipit: Populo tuo, quaesumus, Domine, adesto propitius
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

translations.text: Receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the gifts we bring you out of your own bounty, that these most holy mysteries, by the working power of your grace, may sanctify us in the conduct of this present life and bring us to everlasting joys. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.incipit: Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur
propers.name: Communion Antiphon

masses.name: Eighteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.incipit: Propitius, Domine, quaesumus, haec dona sanctifica
propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

translations.text: Graciously sanctify these gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, and, accepting the offering of this spiritual sacrifice, make us ourselves an everlasting gift to you. Through Christ our Lord.

Attend with unfailing protection, O Lord, those whom you refresh with the gift of heaven, and grant that they whom you never cease to cherish may be made worthy of everlasting redemption. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Nineteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.incipit: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, quem, docente Spiritu Sancto
propers.name: Collect

propers.incipit: Ecclesiae tuae, Domine, munera placatus assume
propers.name: Prayer over the Offerings

translations.text: Receive with favour, O Lord, the gifts of your Church, which in your mercy you gave her to offer, and which by your power you make pass over into the mystery of our salvation. Through Christ our Lord.

propers.incipit: Sacramentorum tuorum, Domine, communio sumpta nos salvet
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

translations.text: May the communion of your sacraments, O Lord, which we have received, save us and strengthen us in the light of your truth. Through Christ our Lord.

masses.name: Twentieth Sunday in Ordinary Time

propers.name: Collect

translations.text: O God, who have prepared unseen good things for those who love you, pour into our hearts the love of you, that loving you in all things and above all things we may obtain your promises, which surpass all desire. Through our Lord.

propers.incipit: Per haec sacramenta, Domine, Christi participes effecti
propers.name: Prayer after Communion

translations.text:
Sion, lift thy voice, and sing;
Praise thy Saviour and thy King;
Praise with hymns thy Shepherd true:
Strive thy best to praise Him well;
Yet doth He all praise excel;
None can ever reach His due.

See to-day before us laid
The living and life-giving Bread!
Theme for praise and joy profound!
The same which at the sacred board
Was, by our Incarnate Lord,
Giv’n to his Apostles round.

Let the praise be loud and high;
Sweet and tranquil be the joy
Felt to-day in every breast;
On this Festival divine,
Which records the origin
Of the glorious Eucharist.

On this Table of the King,
Our new Paschal offering
Brings to end the olden rite;
Here, for empty shadows fled,
Is Reality instead;
Here, instead of darkness, Light.

His own act, at supper seated,
Christ ordain’d to be repeated,
In His Memory divine;
Wherefore now, with adoration,
We the Host of our salvation
Consecrate from bread and wine.

Hear what holy Church maintaineth,
That the bread its substance changeth
Into Flesh, the wine to Blood.
Doth it pass thy comprehending?
Faith, the law of sight transcending,
Leaps to things not understood.

Here, beneath these signs, are hidden
Priceless things, to sense forbidden;
Signs, not things, are all we see;—
Flesh from bread, and Blood from wine;
Yet is Christ, in either sign,
All entire, confess’d to be.

They too, who of Him partake,
Sever not, nor rend, nor break,
But entire, their Lord receive.
Whether one or thousands eat,
All receive the self-same meat,
Nor the less for others leave.

Both the wicked and the good
Eat of this celestial Food;
But with ends how opposite!
Here ’tis life; and there ’tis death;
The same, yet issuing to each
In a difference infinite.

Nor a single doubt retain,
When they break the Host in twain,
But that in each part remains
What was in the whole before;
Since the simple sign alone
Suffers change in state or form,
The Signified remaining One
And the Same for evermore.

Lo! upon the Altar lies,
Hidden deep from human eyes,
Bread of Angels from the skies,
Made the food of mortal man:
Children’s meat to dogs denied;
In old types foresignified;
In the manna Heav’n-supplied,
Isaac, and the Paschal Lamb.

Jesu! Shepherd of the sheep!
Thou thy flock in safety keep.
Living Bread! thy life supply;
Strengthen us, or else we die;
Fill us with celestial grace:
Thou, who feedest us below!
Source of all we have or know!
Grant that with thy Saints above,
Sitting at the feast of love,
We may see Thee face to face.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts, and guidance/propers-for-agents.md
reserves the choice among them to the maintainer. This row records that the
maintainer named Caswall; it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Same transcription as the 1962 row; the two Latin texts are the same twenty-four strophes. The Missal notes that the Sequence is optional and that the shorter form may begin at `Ecce panis Angelorum`: that strophe is Caswall's eleventh stanza, which this printing marks with the bracketed `[Ecce panis angelorum.]` at its head, so the shorter form is this text's last two stanzas and needs no further reading.

differ materially over these five texts, and guidance/propers-for-agents.md

maintainer named Caswall; it does not argue that Caswall is right.

Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
